info.title: Gateward API
info.description: Multi-tenant identity provider — core auth, admin, API keys, and event querying.

get.summary:
ARCH-001: JWKS endpoint publishing the public keys of all active
signing key pairs. Unauthenticated — this is public key material
that any token verifier needs to validate signatures.
get.description:
ARCH-002: Cache-Control header tells clients/CDNs to cache the JWKS
for 1 hour (keys rotate on a much slower cadence — days/weeks, not
minutes). `public` allows shared caches; `max-age=3600` bounds it.

get.summary: Platform admin event query — no app_id scoping, all events visible.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `created_at` (RFC 3339, e.g. last-24h queries).

get.summary:
Feedback #5: expose the scope catalog so the dashboard loads it
dynamically instead of hardcoding a list that can drift from the Core.

delete.summary:
OPS-001: admin can revoke any session, not just their own. The
actor_id is logged so the audit trail records who revoked it.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by account status (e.g. `blocked`) — server-side so the
dashboard doesn't fetch everything to show blocked users.

patch.summary:
OPS-001 / AUDIT-STATUS-001: block, ban, or reactivate a user. `blocked`
(temporary) and `banned` (permanent) require a `reason` (§13.4) and
proactively revoke all active sessions — the access token TTL is 15 min,
so this is the difference between "eventual" and "immediate" enforcement
(CORE-006). Does NOT touch `locked_until` (the lockout system's field).

400.description: Invalid status, or missing reason for block/ban

patch.summary:
Operator annotations at the identity level — set from the dashboard when
someone investigates a user and wants to record notes/tags/behavior.
Distinct from the per-app `local_metadata` an app writes about its own user.

400.description: metadata must be a JSON object

403.description: Not platform admin, and not app:user_manage on this app
Not platform admin, and not app:user_manage on this app

404.description: No membership for that user in this app

patch.summary:
Bootstrapping: the first `app_admin` of an app is promoted by a platform
admin (there is nobody with `app:user_manage` inside the app yet).
patch.description:
The target's live access token keeps its old scopes until it expires or
refreshes — scopes are re-derived at `/v1/auth/refresh` (scopes.rs).

403.description: Not platform admin, and not app:user_manage on this app

404.description: No membership for that user in this app

409.description: Would leave the app without an app_admin

delete.summary:
PROVISION-DELETE-001: hard-delete an app for wizard cleanup. Refuses if
the app still has memberships, sessions, API keys, or events (409) —
those must be removed first (protects against deleting a live app).

patch.summary:
APP-POLICY-001: `password_policy` and `require_email_verification` are
product decisions per app, so they need a way in. Every field is
optional — a PATCH only touches what it names.

post.summary:
SELF-001: change your own password while logged in. Unlike
forgot/reset-password (§11), authorization here is the access token
plus proof of the current password — no email round-trip.
post.description:
Every *other* session in the identity_pool is revoked; the caller's
own stays alive, since logging someone out of the screen they just
used to change their password is hostile, not safer.

400.description: Weak password or same as current

401.description: Not authenticated or wrong current password

post.summary:
Plan V6 §11.1/§13.2: identical response whether or not the email
exists in this identity_pool.

parameters.name: X-Gateward-App-Id
parameters.description: App ID the user belongs to

202.description: Reset email sent (or email doesn't exist)

post.summary:
Plan V6 §4.1/§13.3. Order matters for anti-enumeration: password and
membership are checked before account_status is ever allowed to
affect the response, so blocked/banned/locked never leak beyond the
same generic error as a bad password.

parameters.name: X-Gateward-App-Id
parameters.description: App ID the user is logging into

get.summary:
SELF-001: who am I. Apps need this right after login/refresh to render
a profile screen without proxying through their own backend with an
API key (which is what `/v1/users/{id}/metadata` forces today).

patch.summary:
SELF-001: write your own per-app metadata (display name, preferences).
Same storage as `PATCH /v1/users/{id}/metadata`, but gated on
`users:write_own` and hard-scoped to the caller's own membership —
the user id is never taken from the request.

400.description: metadata must be a JSON object

403.description: Missing users:write_own scope or no app-scoped session

404.description: No membership in the caller's app

post.summary:
Plan V6 §7.13: platform admins live in the system identity_pool and
aren't scoped to any app, so this is a dedicated login path rather
than the app-scoped /v1/auth/login (CORE-001).

Plan V6 §13.1: the same response whether the email was new or already
existed in this identity_pool, and login happens as a separate call.
post.description:
APP-POLICY-001 gives an app an opt-out: with
`require_email_verification = false` the user is created active and
registration returns tokens directly. That trades away §13.1's
anti-enumeration property — a duplicate email gets no tokens, which is
observable — so it's an explicit per-app decision, off by default.

parameters.name: X-Gateward-App-Id
parameters.description: App ID the user is registering into

202.description: Registration accepted (or email already exists). Carries tokens when the app does not require email verification

post.summary:
Plan V6 §12/§13: identical response whether the email doesn't exist,
is already verified, or genuinely got a new token — never reveals
which case applies.

parameters.name: X-Gateward-App-Id
parameters.description: App ID the user belongs to

post.summary:
Plan V6 §11.2/§11.3: revokes every active session for the user
within its identity_pool once the password changes. No AppContext
needed — token possession is the authorization, and the token
already carries its own ecosystem/pool/app.
Plan V6 §12. No AppContext needed — same reasoning as reset_password.

delete.summary:
PROVISION-DELETE-001: hard-delete an ecosystem for Setup Wizard cleanup.
Refuses to delete the system ecosystem, or one that still has identity
pools, apps, or users (409) — the caller must remove children first.

409.description: System ecosystem, or has dependent resources

get.summary:
AUTHZ-002: app-scoped event query. Service accounts with
`events:read_app` see only their own app's events. Platform admins
get the full view. If a non-admin passes an app_id filter, it must
match their token's app_id (cross-app enforcement).

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `created_at` (RFC 3339, e.g. last-24h queries).

200.description: List of events (scoped to caller's app for service accounts)

403.description: Missing events:read_app scope or not platform admin

post.summary:
Plan V6 §18.1 `sendEvent`. Service accounts with `events:write` emit
custom app events. The ecosystem/pool/app are taken from the caller's
credential — never the body — so an app can only write into its own
scope (cross-app safe). `event_type` must be namespaced (contain a
`.`), which keeps app events from colliding with the Core's internal
snake_case audit events (§11.2/§15) — none of which contain a `.`.

delete.summary:
PROVISION-DELETE-001: hard-delete an identity pool for wizard cleanup.
Refuses the system pool, or one that still has apps or users (409).

409.description: System pool, or has dependent apps/users

parameters.name: include_current
parameters.description:
Whether to also revoke the session making the request. Defaults to
false — "log out everywhere else" is the common case, and the SDK
can still call `/v1/auth/logout` for the current one.

ClientInfo.description:
Typed view of the `client_info` jsonb stored on a session / event — so the
OpenAPI contract exposes real properties instead of an opaque object.
Mirrors the fields [`ClientContext::to_metadata`] writes (all optional; only
present fields are serialized).

CoreEventMetadata.description:
Documented shape of `EventRecord.metadata` for events the Core emits
itself (item #7 in dashboard feedback). Not the runtime type of `metadata`
— that stays free-form `Value` because custom app events define their own
keys — but a typed reference the dashboard can cast to. All fields optional;
which appear depends on `event_type`.

keys.description: Top-level keys touched by a metadata patch (`*_metadata_updated`).

target_email.description: Target user's email on admin status changes.

expires_at.description:
Optional expiry (RFC 3339). Omit for a non-expiring key. Must be in
the future; the Core rejects the key on every use once it passes.

oneOf.description:
APP-POLICY-001. Omitted means the Core default (min 8, max 128, no
character-class requirements).

require_email_verification.description:
Whether registration leaves the account unverified and email-gated.
Omitted means `true` — the historical behaviour.

metadata.description:
Free-form JSON. Custom app events carry arbitrary keys; Core-emitted
events (`admin_*`, `login_*`, `*_metadata_updated`, `api_key_*`) carry
the well-known shape documented by [`CoreEventMetadata`] — the dashboard
can narrow to it by `event_type`.

Jwk.description:
JWK as published in the JWKS endpoint. RFC 7517 §4.
`crv = "P-256"`, `kty = "EC"`, `alg = "ES256"` for ES256 keys.

since.description: Inclusive lower bound on `created_at` (RFC 3339, e.g. last-24h queries).

oneOf.description:
Filter by account status (e.g. `blocked`) — server-side so the
dashboard doesn't fetch everything to show blocked users.

Role in the caller's app — `null` for a platform-admin session,
which isn't scoped to an app.

metadata.description:
The caller's own `app_memberships.local_metadata` — `{}` when the
session isn't app-scoped.

PasswordPolicy.description:
APP-POLICY-001: per-app password rules, stored as `apps.password_policy`.
The defaults reproduce what `register.rs` hardcoded before this existed.

numeric_only.description:
Digits only — a PIN. Mutually exclusive with the `require_upper` /
`require_symbol` flags, which no digit string can ever satisfy.

metadata.description: JSON object shallow-merged into the caller's own `local_metadata`.
JSON object shallow-merged into the membership's `local_metadata`.

RegisterResponse.description:
One shape for both outcomes: `message` is always present, and the token
fields appear only when the app has `require_email_verification = false`
(APP-POLICY-001) — so an SDK reads the same type either way.

scopes.description: The catalog of scopes a service-account API key may be granted.

event_type.description:
Namespaced event type, e.g. `app.checkout.completed`. Must contain
a `.` and use `[a-z0-9._-]` only.

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON object with event details.

user_id.description:
Optional user this event is about. If set, must belong to the
caller's identity pool.

UpdateAppRequest.description: Every field optional: a PATCH only touches what it names.

reason.description:
Required when blocking/banning (Plan V6 §13.4). Stored on the user and
recorded in the event; cleared when reactivating.

status_reason.description: Why the account is blocked/banned (AUDIT-STATUS-001). Null when active.
